question.sit: You have the puck and your teammate is skating up the middle with no one near them. A defender is reaching for you. What is the best play?
opts: Pass it to your open teammate in the middle
Hold onto it and try to skate around the defender
Shoot it all the way down the ice
Stop and wait for help
question.explain: An open teammate with speed up the middle is the best option. A good pass beats a stickhandle when a defender is already on you.

proxyVerdict.rationale: On-brand 'what's the read' framing, one clean decision, friendly for U7-U9. Good teaser value.

question.sit: You carry the puck on a 2-on-1. The lone defender slides over and takes away the pass to your teammate. What is the highest-value decision?
opts: Shoot — the defender committed to the pass, so the lane to the net is open
Force the pass through the defender anyway
Turn back to your own end and regroup
Dump the puck into the corner
question.explain: When the defender commits to taking away the pass, they have given you the shooting lane. Reading what the defender takes away tells you what is open.

proxyVerdict.rationale: Anchor decision-making content, textbook 'read what the D gives you' — exactly the RinkReads core. Strong.

question.sit: 3-on-2 rush. You are the middle driver without the puck. The puck carrier is wide on the right. What should you do?
opts: Drive hard to the net for a pass or rebound
Curl back toward the blue line
Stop at the top of the circles and wait
Skate to the same side as the puck carrier
question.explain: On a 3-on-2 the middle lane drives the net — it forces the defence to honour you and opens a pass or a rebound. Spreading the attack stretches two defenders across three lanes.

proxyVerdict.rationale: Covers the odd-man gap the coaches flagged; off-puck 'where do I go' read. Multi-age (U11+U13) is good coverage value.

question.sit: You are the lone defender on a 2-on-1. The puck carrier is winding up to shoot. What is your job?
opts: Take away the pass and let your goalie have the shot
Slide to block the shot and leave the pass open
Skate at the puck carrier to try a poke check
Back all the way in to the net
question.explain: On a 2-on-1 the defender takes away the pass and trusts the goalie to handle the shot. A shooter the goalie can see is a better outcome than a back-door tap-in.

proxyVerdict.rationale: Defensive mirror of the 2-on-1 read; teaches the trust-the-goalie principle. Pairs well with the offensive odd-man item.
